newsitem.title: ITALY: Crashed car legend Bugatti starts selling assets.
newsitem.headline: Crashed car legend Bugatti starts selling assets.

text.p: Fewer than expected fans of legendary Italian racing car maker Bugatti turned out on Friday for a special auction of assets of the crashed company.

Some 40 people turned up at a courtroom in the northern Italian town of Modena to witness the sale, but only seven of the 14 lots on offer found a buyer despite 26 sealed bids -- well below the receivers' expectations.
The sale, which included six Bugatti cars that never made it into the showrooms, raised four billion lire ($2.4 million).
The only thing not on offer was the actual Bugatti marque, which is owned by Luxembourg-based Bugatti International -- itself under court administration.
Officials said a second sale was likely to be organised for the lots which were left unsold.
Bugatti, founded by Ettore Bugatti in 1909, was the biggest racing car manufacturer between the two world wars and made some of the most expensive and coveted collectors' cars.

Bugatti stopped production in the 1950s but started up again in 1989 when Italian entrepreneur Romano Artioli bought the dormant marque, reviving it as a 350 kph (250 mph) supercar, manufacturing the exotic vehicles at some $300,000 each.
The firm failed to find enough buyers and collapsed under the weight of its debt in 1995.
Despite its cult status, no buyer for the company emerged and the receivers were called in. The asset sale was arranged after lengthy attempts to salvage the firm collapsed.
